name: project_open
description: Open a project by name (one of the four sample projects or one of the user's own) and show its Project window: 'open the drone project', 'let's work on the rocket', 'open my classifier'. Takes the name as said: an alias like drone, quad, quadcopter, truck, car, rocket, classifier or model, or a project's title. The answer has the project's loop of steps (which are available, and why not) and next_step with a say line: offer that step to the user in your own words. A sample project (RC truck, Quadcopter, Rocket, Image classifier) is a worked example with some history already: the answer says sample true and what it shows; offer to explore it, keep going, or copy it with project_copy.

name.description: The project as the user said it ('drone', 'the RC truck', 'my rover'), or an id like proj_quadcopter.

name: project_step
description: Do one step of the open project's loop, the same as tapping it in the Project window: RC truck course, drive, train, autopilot, code; Quadcopter design, course, fly, train, autopilot; Rocket design, simulate, launch; Image classifier and other ML projects data, train, results, publish. Without step it does the next step. Every project also has send, which only drafts its latest result to the project's channel for the user to Send or Cancel. Publish only reads back what would go on GitHub; the user confirms to Albie before anything is pushed. A step that isn't available answers why.

step.description: The step to do. Default: the next step.

name: project_copy
description: Make the user's own copy of a sample project and open it: 'copy the rocket', 'make my own truck from the sample'. The copy is titled 'My <sample>' and keeps the sample's plan and design link but none of its history (versions, runs, notes); the sample stays as it is. Only the four sample projects can be copied. Without name it copies the open project.

name.description: The sample as the user said it ('the truck', 'quadcopter'), or an id like proj_rocket. Default: the open project.
